name: COSI
summary: COSI is a selected NASA SMEX gamma-ray mission for a proposed low Earth orbit. A historical prototype flew by balloon from Wanaka, New Zealand, in 2016; balloon and future satellite phases are distinguished here.
detection_principle: Cryogenic germanium detectors measure successive Compton-scattering positions and energies to reconstruct gamma-ray images, line spectra and polarization with high spectral resolution. Dark-matter studies require Galactic-continuum and astrophysical-line background models.

results.summary: The balloon prototype completed a flight and validated technology; it is not evidence of current satellite data taking.
Recent studies forecast COSI's sensitivity to MeV dark-matter decay; no satellite dark-matter results yet.

science_scope: Searches cosmic gamma-ray, antiparticle or neutrino spectra, directions and fluxes for indirect signatures of dark-matter annihilation, decay or related new physics. Conventional astrophysical sources and propagation can produce similar signals, requiring background modeling; design sensitivity is not a measured limit or discovery.
